text: Thornridge Insurance has run its claims database on the same on-prem server for thirteen years. Three weeks ago, a disk failure came within hours of taking the whole array down. This series follows the migration that scare finally funded.
One disk failed in an eight-disk array Friday night. A second disk in the same mirrored pair logged failure warnings five hours later -- one more failure from losing the array entirely.
Backups were current, so real exposure stayed under fifteen minutes. But a full restore had never been tested end to end, and the documented runbook pointed at a path that moved years earlier.
IT, Claims Operations, and the DBA who'd kept this server running for over a decade all confirmed this account before one requirement got written.
The scare is documented. Next: turning 'make this reliable' into a requirement you can actually test.
